title: Ezekiel Bible Quiz - Chapter 5
description: Ten questions on Ezekiel 5: the sword used as a razor, the hair divided in three, and the judgments spoken over Jerusalem.

questions.text: What was he to take and use as a barber's razor over his head and beard?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:1 tells him to take a sharp sword and use it as a barber's razor over his head and over his beard.

answers.text: A sharp knife of flint
A pair of shears
A sharp sword
A burning coal

questions.text: What was he to do with the hair after it was cut off?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:1 says he was to take balances to weigh and divide the hair.

answers.text: Burn all of it at once
Bury it outside the city
Give it to the elders of Judah
Weigh it in balances and divide it

questions.text: What was to be done with the three parts of the hair?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:2 says a third part was to be burned in the fire in the middle of the city, a third struck with the sword around it, and a third scattered to the wind.

answers.text: One third burned, one third struck with the sword, one third scattered to the wind
All of it burned in the fire outside the city
One third buried, one third sold and one third kept hidden
One third given to the priests and the rest scattered abroad

questions.text: Where was he to bind a few of the hairs?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:3 tells him to take a few in number and bind them in the folds of his robe.

answers.text: In a clay jar
In the folds of his robe
Around the iron pan
In a hole in the wall

questions.text: Which city does the Lord Yahweh point to and say he has set her in the middle of the nations?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:5 says, "This is Jerusalem. I have set her in the middle of the nations, and countries are around her."

answers.text: Samaria
Babylon
Tyre
Jerusalem

questions.text: What does the Lord Yahweh say she has done more than the nations around her?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:6 says she has rebelled against his ordinances in doing wickedness more than the nations, and against his statutes more than the countries around her.

answers.text: Gathered more wealth than all of them
Built more cities than those around her
Rebelled against his ordinances in doing wickedness
Offered more sacrifices than all of them

questions.text: What does he say the fathers and the sons will do within her?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:10 says the fathers will eat the sons within her, and the sons will eat their fathers.

answers.text: They will flee together to the mountains
The fathers will eat the sons and the sons their fathers
They will all be sold to the nations as slaves
They will turn against their own prophets

questions.text: What reason does he give in verse 11 for diminishing her?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:11 says that because she defiled his sanctuary with all her detestable things and abominations, he will also diminish her, and his eye will not spare.

answers.text: She defiled his sanctuary with her detestable things
She refused to pay tribute to the nations
She trusted in Egypt for help
She forgot the names of her fathers

questions.text: What does he say will happen to the three parts of the people?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:12 says a third will die with the pestilence and be consumed with famine, a third will fall by the sword around her, and a third he will scatter to all the winds.

answers.text: All of them will be carried away to Babylon together
A third will be spared inside the sanctuary walls
A third by pestilence and famine, a third by the sword, a third scattered
Two thirds will escape to the mountains and live there

questions.text: What does Yahweh say he will send on them in verse 17?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 5:17 says he will send famine and evil animals, pestilence and blood will pass through them, and he will bring the sword on them.

answers.text: Rain, hail and a great storm from the north
Famine, evil animals, pestilence and blood, and the sword
Locusts, darkness and a cloud over the land
Peace, plenty and rest from their enemies
